title: xout — rules your coding agent actually follows
description: Cross out the wrong coding-agent behavior; xout compiles the survivors into rules and plugs them into Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Copilot, pi, Kiro, or any tool that reads AGENTS.md.
social_image_alt: The agent behavior “Should I start?” is crossed out in red while “Fixed. Tests pass.” compiles into “Act first. Report after.”
hero_title: Cross out the agent behavior you never want again.
hero_body: Every AI coding tool follows a rules file, and almost nobody writes a good one. xout shows two concrete ways your agent could act - across a bugfix, a new feature, and a risky migration. You cross out the wrong one; xout writes the rules and plugs them into the tool you use: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Copilot, pi, Kiro, or anything that reads AGENTS.md.
proof_line: 15 cross-outs · three scenes (two routine, one irreversible) · all eight axes strike-backed · one-line enable and rollback
first_screen_notice: Sessions run in English with --lang en (Japanese and Chinese: --lang ja / zh, shipping with the next release); the default is Korean. The event ledger is language-neutral either way.
demo_summary: Watch a real 15-strike terminal session (0.6 MB GIF)
demo_alt: A real xout terminal session progressing through fifteen strikes, compiling eight conditional rules, and applying them with one keystroke.
storyboard_accessible: Story: Input “Fix the bug.” Two behaviors appear: “Should I start?” is crossed out; “Fixed. Tests pass.” survives without approval. xout generates “Act first on reversible changes; confirm first on irreversible ones.” The next response is “Fixed. Tests pass. Here is what changed.”
storyboard_followup: The storyboard above is a complete example; animation is decorative.
story_rule: Act first on reversible changes; confirm first on irreversible ones.
story_next: Fixed. Tests pass. Here is what changed.
mechanism_title: One red line removes a behavior. The survivor becomes an instruction.
mechanism_intro: Compare two concrete responses to the same coding task. Cross out the one you do not want repeated.
how_it_works_alt: Animation: a circle of 6,561 possible agents is cut in half eight times, one axis per cut, until the thinnest slice is left; it becomes eight rules plugged into your tool's rules file.
how_it_works_caption: Every X cuts what's left in half and drops the half you never want. Eight cuts, eight rules, plugged into your tool.
left_transcript: Before fixing pagination, ask whether tests and cleanup are in scope.
right_transcript: Fix pagination, run focused tests, then report the change and evidence.
rail_caption: The counter shows remaining candidates. XOUT.md and manifest.json show the behavior and evidence you actually chose - and `xout why` traces every rule back to your X's.
rule_text: Write a short plan first, then proceed immediately. However, for hard-to-reverse work like deletes, pushes, deploys, and migrations, always get approval before executing.
outcome_title: Turn a recurring agent annoyance into a rule.
outcome_intro: Give the same request before and after enabling xout. The compiled rule changes the behavior your agent's next session is instructed to follow.
outcome_after: Fixed. Tests pass. Here is what changed.
outcome_xout: Executable rules, plugged into each tool's own rules file with one owned line or block.
outcome_manifest: Evidence and source ledger for every decision.
outcome_settings: Reviewable proposal; nothing activates until you enable it.
outcome_activation: Enable with one line; rollback with one line by removing xout’s owned import.
outcome_axes: Eight strike-backed axes: autonomy, scope, test discipline, documentation, error handling, commit policy, verification before done, and dependency policy. Five are measured in both routine and irreversible scenes - when your strikes diverge, the rule compiles with that condition attached.
start_title: Open your first behavior comparison locally.
quickstart_body: One command in your terminal, or let your agent run the session as a conversation: inside Claude Code, /xout:xout shows each pair in chat and records only your explicit choice.
quickstart_note: Finish 15 cross-outs, apply with one keystroke, then repeat the same request in a fresh session of your agent. Ask `xout why` for the receipts, `xout probe` to check the rules hold, `xout undo` to take everything back.
plugin_install_summary: Install as a checksum-verified Claude Code plugin
step_one_body: Download the plugin ZIP, SHA256SUMS, and verifier together. Verify before extracting into a fresh versioned directory; the README includes PowerShell.
step_two_body: Install the extracted package from your local marketplace.
step_three_body: Run the session as a conversation: the agent shows each behavior pair in chat, you pick the one to X, and it records only your explicit choice. Then enable the rule import and inspect status.
boundaries_title: Useful because the edges are explicit.
boundary_local_body: Your files, your install, your decision to activate.
boundary_runtime_title: No runtime LLM, external network, or telemetry
boundary_runtime_body: The whole session runs inside your terminal; it makes no model call, remote request, or analytics trail.
boundary_replay_body: Recorded strikes stay ordered and replay to the same result.
boundary_activation_body: Enable only when ready; rollback removes only xout's owned import line.
boundary_recheck_body: Review whether the rule still fits after a week; survival is unmarked, never approval.
share_title: A short sentence, backed by the README.
share_sentence: You cross out the wrong behavior; xout compiles the survivor into a local rule.
footer_note: Built for inspectable, local coding-agent behavior rules.
